newsitem.title: GERMANY: Jewish cemetery desecrated in Cologne.
newsitem.headline: Jewish cemetery desecrated in Cologne.

text.p: A Jewish cemetery in the western city of Cologne was desecrated by knocking over yombstones and spraying them with swastikas, German police said on Monday.
Five gravestones had been knocked over and sprayed with white paint and fifteen had been sprayed with swastikas, the Nazi symbol banned in Germany, and with the Star of David.
German police said it was unclear when the attack took place and how the assailants scaled the surrounding 2.5 metre (8 ft 2 in) wall.

The incident was the latest in a series of attacks on Jewish cemeteries and monuments since German unification in 1990. In October last year there was a whole spate of attacks on Jewish graveyards and monuments.
A Berlin memorial for Jews deported to the Nazi death camps was vandalised three times in the same week and eight plaster statues forming a temporary Holocaust memorial in Berlin were partly smashed.
Vandals desecrated a Jewish cemetery in eastern Germany by daubing the entrance with Nazi slogans and spraying a marble commemorative plaque with a swastika in October as well.
Earlier last year, on the eve of end-of-World War Two celebrations, vandals in a district of east Berlin toppled 103 tombstones in a part of a cemetery reserved for victims of Adolf Hitler's regime.
